name: Via Current & Thermal
blurb: current a via array carries and its temperature rise from drill, plating and count
intro: How much current a group of plated vias carries for an allowed temperature rise, how hot it runs at your current, its resistance, and how well it conducts heat through the board. Current comes from the IPC-2221 conductor chart applied to the via's barrel wall; heat from plain conduction along copper.

inputs.label: Barrel plating thickness
inputs.help: IPC-6012 average: class 2 20 µm, class 3 25 µm. Budget fabs often plate ~18 µm.

inputs.label: Via length
inputs.help: Board thickness for a through via.

inputs.label: Heat to move through the board
inputs.help: Optional: e.g. a regulator's loss under its thermal pad.

examples.title: Thermal pad of a 2 W regulator, 9 vias

usage: Give drill diameter in mm, plating in µm, via length in mm, via count, total current in A, allowed temperature rise in °C (and optionally watts of heat to conduct through the board). Returns current per via and for the array at that rise, the rise at your current, vias needed, resistance and voltage drop, and thermal resistance per via and for the array in K/W, plus tables by via count and drill size. Use it to size power-path via arrays and thermal-pad via fields.
sources: IPC-2221B Generic Standard on Printed Board Design, section 6.2 and figure 6-4 (conductor current vs. temperature rise, I = k ΔT^0.44 A^0.725)
IPC-6012 Qualification and Performance Specification for Rigid Printed Boards (minimum hole wall copper, class 2 and 3)
Copper resistivity 1.724e-8 Ω·m at 20 °C and 0.00393/°C (IACS); copper thermal conductivity 385 W/m·K
